minimum_answer: Failure example: a=[1,2], t=2. Trace: l=0,r=1,m=0; a[0]=1<2 so l=0; loop condition l<r still holds, so it repeats forever (no progress). Repair: use half-open interval [l,r) with l=0, r=len(a); while l<r: m=(l+r)//2; if a[m]<t: l=m+1 else r=m; return l. This keeps O(log n) because each iteration strictly shrinks r-l. Termination: r-l decreases every iteration (either l increases past m or r becomes m), so the loop ends. Correctness: maintain invariant that all indices <l have a[i]<t and all indices >=r have a[i]>=t (or r=len(a)); when l==r, l is the first index with a[l]>=t, or len(a) if none. Duplicates and t above all entries are handled because the invariant covers all positions.
